newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Aug 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The AMP Society is seeking permission from the Insurance and Superannuation Commission to become its own largest individual shareholder, possibly breaching the five per cent individual share holding ownership limit, as its subsidiary AMP Superannuation Lt is about to be allocated a large number of shares through its ownership of thousands of superannuation policies. Page 21.

A 63 per cent fall in profits for nickel producer QNI Ltd in 1996-97 has been attributed to a volatile nickel market and bad weather. The profit fall from A$85.9 million to A$32.1 million over the year ending June 30 was in line with market expectations.Page 21.

Meridian Investment Trust shareholders were sent a memorandum yesterday saying they will receive a A$0.10 annual dividend following the company's settlement of litigation resulting from the collapse of the Estate Mortgage trust. Tyndall Funds Management managing director Michael Wilkins says the company is better off settling the case rather than facing years of litigation. Page 22.

A study by Coopers & Lybrand and the Australian Centre for Retail Studies titled Retail Meter 97 reveals that Australian retailers are too optimistic about their future and could face stock overruns and poor financial results. The survey of retailers also revealed that 85 per cent of respondents thought they would outperform the general retail market in the 1997/98 financial year. Page 22.

Trucking group Finemore Holdings Ltd managing director Ron Finemore says he is unhappy about the company's fiscal performance for the 1996/97 financial year, which saw a 17.3 per cent fall in net profits. Finemore believes however, the company's profits wll improve in the coming year as it is well placed for acquisitions. Page 22.

Manettas Ltd directors are set to ask shareholders to approve a name change for the company to Bidvest Australia Ltd, after major South African shareholder Bidvest which owns 51 per cent of the company. the name change is designed to reflect the company's new direction from seafood to food services. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Asia-Pacific sharemarkets definitely felt the repercussion from the dramatic Wall Street fall on Friday but not as severely as expected. The Tokyo Nikkel 225 index fell by 284.93 points to finish at 19,041.1 and the Singapore Straits Times Industrials indx fell by 34.95 points to 1918.85. London's FTSE 100 index also fell by 80 points during trading yesterday but recovered to finish 33 points down at 4829. Page 21.

Australian Stock Exchange chief Richard Humphry reassured investors yesterday that the stock market crash of 1987 would not be repeated as concerns grew over the possible fallout from Friday's Wall Street slide. Humphry said he was expecting a drop of 50 or 60 points, in response to the United States sharemarket drop. Page 21.

The Federal Government has been told by three of the world's largest drug companies that pharmaceutical investment in Australia is under threat if the Government does not change drug pricing rules. Overseas companies also blame a lack of consultation for the negative effect of the Therapeutic Group Premiums scheme, announced in the Budget. page 21.

Three of Merrill Lynch's most senior executives came to Sydney to review investment banking business McIntosh & Co and found their newly acquired group has been called to appear before the Corporations and Securities Panel and may face a possible declaraton of unacceptable conduct for its trading in John Fairfax shares. Page 21.

It appears likely the Australian Securities Commission will form the view that New Zealand's Brierley Investments and Merrill Lynch formed an understanding over a share swap in John Fairfax Holdings. Brierley Investments has reacted angrily, denying claim the company was involved in unacceptable conduct, with Merrill Lynch stating they are confident of the company's legal position. Page 22.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston is set to take his fourth proposal for changes to media ownership regulations to Federal Government backbenchers next week continuing his push for legislative changes. It is believed Alston's new plan involve lifting both cross-media and foreign ownership regulations. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Goldminer Sons of Gwalia have led the way in reassessment of the carrying value of their gold projects and reserves following the recent plunge in gold prices. Other companies are following, realising carrying some of its gold assets is just not realisic. Gwalia, usually considered one of the more conservative gold companies, was prompted to reassess by its recent expansion through acquisition. Page 25.

China plans to transform tens of thousands of State enterprises into shareholding firms. About 35 percent of China's state-owned enterprises have debts greater than their assets, however the public sector employs more than 100 million people. Page 26.

Japan's trade surplus was lower than expected for the month of July, but while it widened, analysts had anticipated higher results. Exports have continued to grow strongly, rising 12.1 per cent in July, while imports only rose by 3.4 per cent. Page 26.

In one of the biggest one-day falls in eight years, Indonesian benchmark stocks yesterday fell by more than eight per cent. Stock prices dropped when trading opened resulting in record panic selling. President Soeharto has announced tight monetary policie will be used to restore stability to the rupiah. Page 26.

Gaming machine manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure has outperformed prospectus forecasts by posting a net profit of A$23.3 million in its first full year on the share market. In 1996 the company made a profit of A$17.8 million. Page 27.

Finemore Holdings trucking group is expecting an abnormal net loss of A$1.37 million, with Finemore's managing director Ron Finemore warning the tough environment was not expected to ease during this financial year. Finemore has managed to keep its operating profit before tax and abnormals at a steady A$14.64 million. Page 27.
THE AGE

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has given no hints about who will replace two Reserve Bank directors Janet Holmes a Court and Solomon Lew, but says that the appointments will be made soon. The Government is expected to look into the business ranks to fil the positions despite recent calls for the board to be distanced from the private sector to reduce conflicts of interest. Page B1.

Following a negative lead set by the United States stock market, the Australian stockmarket fell 1.8 per cent yesterday. The market opened weakly as expected but after the first half hour of trade a spurt of panic selling by retail investors set in. Page B1.

American shares remain high despite having fallen almost seven percent in the last week, with the American market up 19 per cent for the year, and 50 per cent above its starting point in 1995. Investors are told that now is a good time to sell. Page B1

Australian businesses are not ready for the year 2000 computer bug according to former Commonwealth Bank systems analyst Robert Middleton. The biggest economic disaster ever seen could result from the lack of preparation for a computer problem that is caused by software that represents dates with abbreviated symbols. Page B3.

A submission by the Property Council of Victoria to the Retail Tenancies Act review may result in small business retailers being given first preference to extend their leases at major shopping centres. Subject to some conditions, small retailers could be given further provisions on top of the five year minimum lease. Page B3.

According to Federal Government sources The Indian-Pacific, The Gahn and The Overlander rail services will be sold this week. The sale of Australian National will be announced by the Government this week, with the consortium led by rail operator Wisconsin Central believed to the favourite. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
